## Pull request overview

Implements the Q2 2026 roadmap items by expanding `@object-ui/types` with multi-tenancy/RBAC/mobile/designer schemas and introducing new runtime packages (`@object-ui/tenant`, `@object-ui/permissions`, `@object-ui/mobile`) plus a new designer plugin (`@object-ui/plugin-designer`).

**Changes:**
- Added new type definition modules (tenant, permissions/RBAC, mobile, designer) and extended `ui-action` with batch/transaction/undo types.
- Introduced new packages for tenant context + resolution, RBAC permission evaluation + guards, and mobile/PWA hooks/utilities.
- Added `plugin-designer` with page/data-model/process/report designer components and a collaboration provider.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 48 out of 49 changed files in this pull request and generated 29 comments.

<details>
<summary>Files not reviewed (1)</summary>

* **pnpm-lock.yaml**: Language not supported
</details>

This file redefines `cn()` locally, but the repo already exports a standard `cn` utility from `@object-ui/components` (used across other packages). Reuse the shared utility to avoid duplicated implementations and keep class merging behavior consistent.

Inline `style` is used to set canvas width/height and grid background. For a Tailwind-first codebase, consider moving these dynamic values to CSS variables (or a wrapper style API) so most styling remains class-based and themeable.
```suggestion
            className={cn(
              'relative',
              canvas.showGrid &&
                'bg-[radial-gradient(circle,hsl(var(--border))_1px,transparent_1px)] bg-[length:20px_20px]'
            )}
```

The page container sizing is done with inline `style` (width/minHeight). Given the Tailwind-first approach, consider using CSS variables for page dimensions and applying them through utility classes/arbitrary values instead of inline styles so theming/overrides are consistent.

`RoleDefinition.permissions` is required by the type, but the evaluator never consults it (roles are only used for inheritance resolution). This creates two sources of truth (role permissions vs `ObjectPermissionConfig.roles`) and can easily drift. Either incorporate `RoleDefinition.permissions` into evaluation or remove it from the role type to avoid confusion.

`TenantScopedQuery` builds filter conditions with `operator: '='`, but the codebase filter operators are typed as `'equals' | 'not_equals' | ...` (see `FilterOperator` / `AdvancedFilterOperator`). Using `'='` breaks type-safety and interoperability with the existing filter/query tooling. Use the canonical operator values and type the filter as the shared filter condition type instead of `Record<string, unknown>[]`.

When `plan` is provided, tenants with `tenant.plan` unset currently pass the guard because the check only runs when `tenantCtx.tenant.plan` is truthy. If `plan` is required, an undefined tenant plan should fail the guard. Also consider typing `plan`/`status` as `TenantPlan`/`TenantStatus` instead of `string` for type safety.

The `double-tap` branch currently triggers on any single tap (it doesn't measure timing between taps), so it's not actually detecting a double-tap. Either implement a proper double-tap detector (store last tap time/position) or remove `double-tap` support until it’s implemented to avoid misleading API behavior.
This file redefines `cn()` locally; the repo standard `cn` is exported from `@object-ui/components`. Using the shared helper avoids duplicated logic and keeps class merging behavior consistent.

This importer records `react` with specifier `19.2.4`, but `packages/tenant/package.json` declares `react: ^19.1.0` in devDependencies. Please sync `pnpm-lock.yaml` with the workspace manifests (run `pnpm install` after changes).

Nodes are positioned with inline `style` left/top. If this is kept, consider centralizing the positioning approach (e.g., translate via CSS vars) to avoid sprinkling inline styles throughout and to make future theming/zooming easier.
```suggestion
                transform: `translate(${node.position.x}px, ${node.position.y}px)`,
```
This file redefines `cn()` locally; the repo standard utility is exported from `@object-ui/components`. Import the shared `cn` to avoid duplicated implementations across plugins.

In `pnpm-lock.yaml`, this importer records `react` with specifier `19.2.4`, but `packages/mobile/package.json` declares `react: ^19.1.0` in devDependencies. This indicates the lockfile is out of sync with the package manifest; regenerate the lockfile with a fresh `pnpm install` (or align the specifier).

Cookie parsing assumes `document.cookie` entries are separated by `'; '` (semicolon + space). Browsers may omit the space, which can cause missed tenant IDs. Split on `';'` and trim each entry before parsing key/value.

Inline `style` is used for canvas sizing and background rendering. To keep styling Tailwind/theme-friendly, consider moving these dynamic values to CSS variables (set once) and use Tailwind classes/arbitrary values instead of inline styles.

`useCallback` is imported but never used, which will fail lint/type-check in strict setups. Remove the unused import to keep the hook module clean.
```suggestion
import { useContext } from 'react';
```

The 'disable' fallback uses inline styles and only blocks pointer events; interactive children may remain keyboard-focusable/activatable, which is an accessibility issue. Prefer applying Tailwind classes and a more complete disabling strategy (e.g., clone known control types to set `disabled`, or also manage focus/tabIndex).

`TenantProviderConfig` includes `resolution`, header/query/cookie names, etc., but `TenantProvider` currently only uses `defaultTenantId`. This makes the config misleading and leaves tenant resolution unimplemented. Either wire `createTenantResolver(config.resolution, ...)` into the provider (and fetch by resolved ID) or remove/relocate the unused config fields.

Inline `style` is used for absolute positioning/sizing of designer components. For consistency with the rest of the UI system and easier overrides, prefer CSS variables + Tailwind arbitrary values/classes rather than per-node inline styles.

Row-level permissions are not actually enforced: when `record` is provided, the code only checks whether any `rowPermissions` entry includes the action, but it never evaluates `rp.filter` against the record. This means records that should be excluded can still be allowed. The evaluator should apply the row filter condition(s) (or return a combined `rowFilter`) and deny if the record doesn't match.

Field and row helpers in `PermissionProvider` iterate only `userRoles`, but `evaluatePermission()` supports role inheritance. This creates inconsistent answers between `check()` and `checkField()`/`getFieldPermissions()`/`getRowFilter()`. Reuse the same effective-role resolution for these helpers so inherited roles behave consistently.

This file redefines `cn()` locally; the repo standard utility is exported from `@object-ui/components`. Importing the shared `cn` reduces duplication and keeps class merging behavior consistent across packages.

This importer records `react` with specifier `19.2.4`, but `packages/permissions/package.json` declares `react: ^19.1.0` in devDependencies. Lockfile appears out of sync with manifests; please regenerate the lockfile after updating package.json specs.

`handleTouchMove` uses `!startYRef.current` as a sentinel check, but `clientY` can legitimately be `0`, which would incorrectly skip pull tracking. Use a nullable sentinel (e.g., `number | null`) or a separate boolean to indicate whether a pull started.

`longPressTimerRef` is typed as `ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>` but initialized with `undefined`, which is not assignable under strict TS settings (and will typically fail type-check). Widen the ref type to include `undefined`/`null` (or initialize with `null`).

`evaluatePermission` is security-critical logic (RBAC + inheritance + row/field restrictions) but the new package currently has no tests. Adding Vitest coverage for allow/deny precedence, role inheritance, row filter enforcement, and default behaviors would help prevent regressions.
